text: Agile methodology is a popular way of managing projects, especially in software development. Instead of planning everything at the start, teams work in short cycles called sprints, usually lasting two to four weeks. Each day, they hold a quick standup meeting to discuss progress and problems. The team keeps a backlog, which is a list of tasks to be done. These tasks are often broken down into user stories, which are simple descriptions of features from the user’s perspective. Because development is iterative, they build a small part, test it, and then improve it in the next sprint. This allows for constant feedback and makes the project more flexible.
